text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The Tallinn city council held a news conference on the suspicious circumstances surrounding the privatisation of apartments in central Tallinn.
- The government has decided to limit the use of cars by state officials.
- The law against corruption, which passed the second reading, sets some limitations on the economic activities of officials.
- Estonia's foreign minister called for more assurances about the continued enlargement of NATO.
- A joint Estonian-French military exercise was disturbed by an unexpected snowstorm. The French platoon and Estonian soldiers practiced shooting and tactics.
- The criminal police has arrested a gang of criminals, who extorted shares from several large enterprises.
- The parliament financial commission calls for a publication of the central bank's audited report.
- The European Parliament recommends that Estonia abolish the death penalty.
- Tallinn teachers will decide next Tuesday whether or not to strike. They are demanding a 12 percent wage hike.
- Broadcasting Union director Urmas Loit was elected chairman of the Press Council, a watchdog for mass media ethics and rights.
- Estonia will not be admitted to the WTO before a system preventing the import and sale of pirated recordings has been introduced.
- Sillamae town council chairman Priit Saksing wants a free trade area set up in the town.
